summary: Model cards communicate model details such as intended use, evaluation results, limitations, and ethical considerations.
They should be accurate, maintained, and tailored to the model and its audience.

questions.hint: A system-level document describes how models, tools, people, and controls work together.

options.text: Documents describing an AI system's components, behavior, safeguards, evaluation, and limitations
A summary limited to one model's parameter count
A record of only user interface colors
A substitute for operational monitoring

summary: System cards describe an integrated AI application, including connected components, intended use, safeguards, and evaluation.
System documentation complements model-level documentation because deployment context changes risk.

questions.hint: It records information about system design, data, evaluation, decisions, and operation.

options.text: Records that describe an AI system's purpose, data, design, evaluation, controls, and changes
The model's generated response only
A document that guarantees safe operation
A collection of undocumented assumptions

summary: AI documentation helps people understand intended use, data, design choices, evaluation, limitations, and operational changes.
It should be kept current and useful for its intended audience.

questions.questionText: Why should AI systems maintain logs?
questions.hint: Logs can support monitoring and reconstruction, but must be proportionate and protected.

options.text: To monitor behavior, investigate incidents, and reconstruct relevant system activity
To store sensitive information indefinitely without access controls
To replace preventive security measures
To guarantee that every event was recorded correctly

summary: Logs provide evidence for operations, investigations, and audits.
Collect only appropriate information and apply retention, integrity, privacy, and access controls.

questions.hint: It concerns meeting applicable requirements for explaining, documenting, or reviewing AI use.

options.text: Meeting relevant obligations for explanations, records, oversight, and review of AI systems
A universal certificate that makes every AI use lawful
Publishing all confidential model details
A method for improving model accuracy only

summary: Explainability compliance involves meeting applicable requirements related to transparency, documentation, decisions, or oversight.
Requirements vary, so the system's purpose, jurisdiction, and affected people must be considered.

questions.hint: Understanding system behavior can help detect misuse or unusual paths, but explanations must not leak secrets.

options.text: It can help investigate anomalous behavior and identify risky pathways while supporting controlled review
It requires exposing credentials to all users
It replaces access control and threat modeling
It guarantees that the model cannot be manipulated

summary: Explanatory traces can help security teams investigate behavior and identify unexpected tool use or inputs.
Explanation access must be controlled to avoid exposing sensitive system details.

questions.hint: Lineage follows data from its source through transformations and use.

options.text: A record of where data came from and how it was transformed and used
A prediction of which data will be collected next year
A method for encrypting a dataset
A list of model outputs without their inputs

summary: Data lineage tracks data provenance and transformations through a system's lifecycle.
It helps with quality checks, rights management, debugging, and audits.

questions.hint: It links a decision to the data, model, rules, and human approvals that influenced it.

options.text: A trace connecting an outcome to relevant inputs, model versions, rules, and review steps
A description of how model weights were initialized only
A guarantee that a decision was fair
A record of employee reporting lines

summary: Decision lineage records the key components and stages contributing to a decision, including human actions where relevant.
It supports reconstruction and review but does not itself establish that the decision was appropriate.

questions.hint: Monitoring checks behavior and performance over time after deployment.

options.text: Ongoing measurement of model performance, data changes, errors, and operational risks
A one-time review before deployment only
A way to prevent any data or behavior change
A dashboard that shows only model age

summary: Model monitoring tracks performance, drift, data quality, safety, and other relevant indicators in production.
Monitoring should have owners and thresholds that trigger investigation or intervention.

questions.questionText: How does explainability help incident investigation?
questions.hint: An investigator needs evidence about inputs, versions, decisions, sources, and actions.

options.text: It can help reconstruct contributing factors and identify where a failure or unsafe action occurred
It guarantees the root cause is obvious from one explanation
It removes the need to preserve logs
It makes all incidents impossible

summary: Explanations and traces can help investigators locate contributing factors and understand a system's path to an outcome.
Root-cause analysis still needs reliable records, technical investigation, and domain context.

questions.hint: Start with the decision, audience, and risk, then choose and validate appropriate methods.

options.text: Define stakeholder needs and risk, select suitable methods, validate explanations, and integrate them into governance
Choose one explanation tool and use it for every model and audience
Add explanations only after an incident
Assume technical transparency alone ensures adoption

summary: Enterprise XAI should begin with use cases, affected stakeholders, and the decisions explanations must support.
Select, evaluate, and govern methods throughout development and deployment, then monitor their value and risk.

questions.hint: Measure whether explanations are faithful, useful, understandable, and used appropriately.

options.text: Indicators such as explanation fidelity, stability, user comprehension, review outcomes, and coverage
A single universal score that proves trustworthiness
The number of words shown in every explanation
Measures limited to model accuracy

summary: XAI KPIs should reflect explanation quality and outcomes, such as fidelity, stability, comprehension, and successful review.
Use metrics appropriate to the users, risk, and decision; no one score captures explainability.

questions.questionText: How can XAI improve business adoption?
questions.hint: Explanations can help teams fit AI outputs into existing decisions and know when to escalate.

options.text: It helps employees understand outputs, verify their basis, and use them with appropriate confidence
It forces employees to automate every decision
It guarantees that users will prefer AI
It replaces workflow and usability design

summary: Well-designed explanations can make AI outputs more actionable and easier to integrate into business processes.
Adoption depends on reliable performance, usability, training, and clear accountability as well.

questions.questionText: How can XAI improve customer service AI?
questions.hint: Customers and support agents benefit from knowing the evidence behind a response and when to escalate.

options.text: Show relevant sources and limits, and make escalation to a human easy
Hide that AI is involved and block human escalation
Present every generated answer as verified fact
Expose another customer's private conversation as evidence

summary: Customer-service explanations can cite approved information, identify uncertainty, and offer a route to human help.
Personal data and access rights must be protected when presenting evidence.

questions.questionText: How can XAI support executive decision making?
questions.hint: Executives need concise evidence, assumptions, uncertainties, and implications rather than raw model internals.

options.text: Summarize relevant drivers, evidence, uncertainty, and limitations for the decision at hand
Show all model parameters without context
Hide uncertainty to simplify the choice
Replace executive accountability with a model score

summary: Executive explanations should communicate decision-relevant evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, and potential impact.
They should be concise without hiding important caveats or the accountable decision-maker.

questions.questionText: What role does explainability play in AI transformation?
questions.hint: Large-scale adoption requires capabilities for oversight and organizational learning, not only models.

options.text: It helps organizations integrate AI with transparent processes, accountable roles, and continuous improvement
It allows an organization to skip change management
It guarantees every AI project will succeed
It requires automating every business process

summary: Explainability supports organizational learning, oversight, and confidence as AI is incorporated into workflows.
Successful transformation also requires data, skills, process design, and sustained governance.

questions.questionText: How do you explain an LLM output to a business user?
questions.hint: Use plain language to summarize what supports the answer, what it cannot establish, and when to verify it.

options.text: Give a concise answer with relevant evidence, important limitations, and a clear way to verify or escalate
Say the model produced it, so no further explanation is needed
Provide a confident rationale without checking its evidence
Reveal confidential technical or customer data unrelated to the question

summary: Explain the answer in business terms and point to relevant evidence, uncertainty, and limitations.
Offer a way to verify or escalate important claims, and avoid exposing unnecessary confidential information.

questions.questionText: What explainability reports should be generated?
questions.hint: Reports should be appropriate for their audience and cover both the model and its use.

options.text: Reports on intended use, data and model provenance, evaluation, explanations, limitations, monitoring, and incidents
A report containing only an accuracy score
The same internal technical report for every audience
Reports that omit known limitations

summary: Useful reports can include system purpose, data lineage, evaluation, explanation quality, limitations, controls, and monitoring results.
The format and detail should fit the audience, from operators to auditors and affected users.

questions.questionText: How should AI decisions be documented?
questions.hint: Keep enough context to reproduce and review a decision without collecting unnecessary sensitive data.

options.text: Record relevant inputs, model and policy versions, evidence, outputs, approvals, and review outcomes
Store only the final answer with no version or context
Keep every user's personal data forever
Rely on the model to remember its past decisions

summary: Decision records should include enough context to support reconstruction, review, and accountability.
Apply data minimization, access controls, retention limits, and integrity protections.

questions.questionText: How can XAI improve user experience?
questions.hint: Give people clear, timely information and a way to verify or question important results.

options.text: Present relevant reasons, evidence, uncertainty, and next steps in an understandable format
Show raw model internals to every user
Hide errors and uncertainty to reduce screen clutter
Require users to read lengthy technical documentation for every result

summary: User-centered explanations make important results easier to understand and act on without overwhelming people.
Use research and testing to tailor detail, terminology, accessibility, and controls.

questions.questionText: Explain the trade-off between accuracy and explainability.
questions.hint: More complex models may perform better on some tasks, while simpler models may be easier to inspect.

options.text: Some tasks involve a trade-off, but it is context-dependent and should be measured rather than assumed
Explainability always reduces accuracy by a fixed amount
Accuracy and explainability are identical measures
A complex model is always both more accurate and more explainable

summary: Complex models can outperform simpler interpretable models on some tasks, but the trade-off varies by data and objective.
Compare task performance, explanation quality, and risk; sometimes an interpretable model performs just as well or better.

questions.questionText: Can a highly explainable model outperform a black-box model?
questions.hint: Performance depends on the task, data, constraints, and evaluation criteria.

options.text: Yes; on some tasks a simpler model can match or exceed a complex one, though results are context-dependent
No; explainable models are always less accurate
Yes; every interpretable model is always more accurate
No; explainability and performance cannot be compared

summary: A highly explainable model can outperform a black-box model when its inductive assumptions fit the task or data well.
The comparison should use representative data and metrics relevant to the actual use.

questions.questionText: How would you explain an LLM response to a regulator?
questions.hint: Describe the system and decision process with traceable evidence, limitations, and controls.

options.text: Document the model and version, prompts, retrieved sources, output checks, uncertainty, controls, and human review
Provide only the model's generated chain of thought as conclusive proof
Claim the model is accurate because it sounds confident
Omit the data and deployment context

summary: A regulator-facing account should be factual and reproducible: explain system purpose, model version, inputs, evidence, controls, evaluation, and review.
Do not present generated reasoning as a guaranteed faithful record; tailor disclosures to applicable obligations.

questions.questionText: How would you explain a hallucinated answer?
questions.hint: Explain how unsupported generation can happen, then identify what evidence and safeguards were missing.

options.text: State that the model generated a plausible but unsupported claim, trace its context, and explain corrective checks
Call it a verified fact because the output was fluent
Blame the user without examining system behavior
Claim that hallucinations cannot occur in a well-designed system

summary: A hallucination should be described as unsupported or inaccurate generated content, with evidence showing what was checked.
Investigate prompt, retrieval, source quality, model behavior, and review controls before drawing conclusions.

questions.questionText: How would you build explainability into a RAG solution?
questions.hint: Make retrieval and generation inspectable, and test whether cited passages actually support claims.

options.text: Record source provenance and retrieved passages, cite claim-level evidence, expose uncertainty, and evaluate grounding
Show citations without checking whether sources support the output
Hide retrieval results and log only the final answer
Assume that retrieval eliminates hallucinations

summary: A transparent RAG design records retrieval queries, source identifiers, passages, model versions, and generated outputs.
Evaluate retrieval quality and claim-to-source support; citations do not guarantee faithful grounding.

questions.questionText: How would you design explainability for an AI agent?
questions.hint: Trace decisions and side effects end-to-end, and include authorization and human approval points.

options.text: Log goals, plans, allowed tools, validated calls, observations, approvals, outcomes, and concise rationales
Expose credentials and raw private reasoning to every user
Record only the final answer and discard actions
Give the agent unrestricted tools and rely on explanations afterward

summary: Agent explainability should make plans, tool calls, evidence, permissions, approvals, and results traceable end-to-end.
Use privacy-aware logs, meaningful human controls, and clear explanations suitable for operators and users.

questions.questionText: How would you audit an LLM decision?
questions.hint: Reconstruct the run using versioned inputs, configuration, sources, outputs, and review records.

options.text: Inspect the use case, model and prompt versions, inputs, retrieval, output, evaluations, controls, and approvals
Ask the same LLM whether it behaved correctly and accept the answer
Review only whether the response was grammatically correct
Audit without preserving any system records

summary: An LLM audit examines system purpose, data and model provenance, prompts, retrieval, outputs, evaluation, access, controls, and human review.
Use independent evidence and assess both expected behavior and relevant failure modes.

questions.questionText: How would you explain a multi-agent workflow?
questions.hint: Describe each agent's role and how information and responsibility move between them.

options.text: Show roles, task routing, handoffs, shared evidence, tool actions, validation, and final responsibility
Show only the final answer from the whole system
Assume every agent independently verified all other agents
Hide agent identities to simplify the audit

summary: Explain the workflow by showing components, delegation, information flow, tool use, checks, and ownership.
The explanation should reveal dependencies and shared failure risks rather than implying that multiple agents guarantee correctness.

questions.questionText: How would you evaluate explanation quality?
questions.hint: Evaluate whether explanations are faithful, stable, understandable, useful, and safe for the audience.

options.text: Measure fidelity, stability, completeness, user comprehension, decision usefulness, and privacy risk
Count words and treat longer explanations as better
Ask only whether users like the visual design
Assume explanation quality is identical to model accuracy

summary: Explanation quality is multidimensional: evaluate fidelity, consistency, comprehensibility, usefulness, and potential harms.
Use task-specific quantitative tests and feedback from relevant users or domain experts.

questions.questionText: What is the future of XAI in Agentic AI ecosystems?
questions.hint: Consider explainability across connected models, tools, data, and autonomous actions.

options.text: More end-to-end, evidence-linked traces and governance that support human oversight across agents and tools
Removing audit trails as agents become more capable
Relying only on longer generated chains of thought
Treating agent autonomy as a substitute for accountability

summary: As agentic systems expand, XAI will need to connect evidence, decisions, tool actions, and outcomes across components.
Reliable progress requires validated explanations, secure traceability, and meaningful human accountability.
